tags.label: Heist
tags.definition: The plot centres on planning and executing a robbery or elaborate scheme.

tags.label: Buddy
tags.definition: An odd-couple partnership drives the story, with bickering as the engine.

tags.label: Dark Comedy
tags.definition: Comedy that treats grim or taboo subject matter with deadpan humour.

tags.label: Mockumentary
tags.definition: Fiction presented as a fake documentary with talking heads and camera gags.

tags.label: Martial Arts
tags.definition: Elaborate hand-to-hand combat is a defining spectacle.

tags.label: Survival
tags.definition: Characters fight to stay alive against nature, wilderness or catastrophe.

tags.label: Disaster
tags.definition: A large-scale catastrophe unfolds across an ensemble cast.

tags.label: Spy
tags.definition: Espionage, agents and intelligence tradecraft drive the plot.

tags.label: Apocalypse
tags.definition: Set during or right after the collapse of civilisation.

tags.label: Prison
tags.definition: Life inside confinement and its inmate hierarchies is central.

tags.label: Investigation
tags.definition: An inquiry into a crime or mystery structures the plot: detectives, sleuths or amateur investigators piece together evidence.

tags.label: Uplifting
tags.definition: The overall emotional tone is warm, hopeful and energising.

tags.label: Melancholic
tags.definition: A sustained sorrowful, wistful emotional tone.

tags.label: Bittersweet
tags.definition: Joy and sadness are deliberately mixed in the emotional payoff.

tags.label: Tense
tags.definition: The emotional tone keeps the viewer on edge for long stretches.

tags.label: Cozy
tags.definition: A comfortable, low-stakes, comforting viewing warmth.

tags.label: Absurd
tags.definition: The tone embraces ridiculous, illogical or surreal comedy.

tags.label: Eerie
tags.definition: An unsettling, quietly menacing emotional undercurrent.

tags.label: Epic
tags.definition: An overwhelming feeling of awe that emotionally sweeps the viewer up, independent of the story's actual scope.

tags.label: Bleak
tags.definition: A harsh, hopeless emotional register with little warmth, comfort or relief in sight.

tags.label: Sentimental
tags.definition: Deliberately tender, heart-on-sleeve emotional appeal that leans into pathos.

tags.label: Dreamlike
tags.definition: The world feels hazy, associative and oneiric rather than literal.

tags.label: Claustrophobic
tags.definition: Tight, enclosed physical spaces press on the characters; the world itself feels cramped and airless.

tags.label: Expansive
tags.definition: Vast landscapes, space or open horizons dominate the world of the film.

tags.label: Urban
tags.definition: Dense city life and its textures define the setting's feel.

tags.label: Rural
tags.definition: Countryside, small settlements and open farmland define the feel.

tags.label: Futuristic
tags.definition: Advanced or imagined future technology shapes the world.

tags.label: Wintry
tags.definition: Snow, cold and long winters define the visual world.

tags.label: Period
tags.definition: The texture of a clearly past historical era defines the world, rather than the present day.

tags.label: World-Building
tags.definition: An elaborate invented world with its own explicit rules and systems takes centre stage.

tags.label: Identity
tags.definition: A central question of who the character is or wants to be.

tags.label: Family
tags.definition: Family bonds, duties and conflicts drive the dramatic stakes.

tags.label: Friendship
tags.definition: Friendship as a key tested value in the story.

tags.label: Coming of Age
tags.definition: A young person's transition to maturity is the core arc.

tags.label: Death and Grief
tags.definition: Loss of a loved one and mourning shape the narrative.

tags.label: Revenge
tags.definition: A vendetta plot structures the major choices.

tags.label: Redemption
tags.definition: A character seeks atonement for past wrongdoing.

tags.label: Obsession
tags.definition: A single fatal fixation dominates a character's will.

tags.label: Corruption
tags.definition: Institutions or individuals rot knowingly under power and money.

tags.label: Technology
tags.definition: Machines, AI or modernisation challenge the human characters.

tags.label: Faith
tags.definition: Religious belief, doubt or spiritual searching is subject matter.

tags.label: Philosophical
tags.definition: The story probes fundamental questions of existence, free will, knowledge or meaning.

tags.label: Moral Ambiguity
tags.definition: Right and wrong stay deliberately blurred; choices carry no clean answers.

tags.label: Class Divide
tags.definition: Tension between social classes and unequal life chances drives the drama.

tags.label: Non-linear
tags.definition: The story is deliberately told out of chronological order.

tags.label: Ensemble
tags.definition: Multiple interwoven storylines and points of view carry the plot.

tags.label: Unreliable Narrator
tags.definition: The audience is misled by a skewed perspective or narrator.

tags.label: Frame Story
tags.definition: A story is told inside another story, with a distinct outer layer.

tags.label: Single Location
tags.definition: The entire story unfolds in essentially one place — a scenario constraint, not a matter of visual tightness.

tags.label: Slow Reveal
tags.definition: Key information is deliberately withheld and disclosed in stages.

tags.label: Episodic
tags.definition: Self-contained episodes accumulate rather than one tight throughline (mainly for series).

tags.label: Character Study
tags.definition: An in-depth portrait of one character's inner life matters more than plot events.

tags.label: Mind Bender
tags.definition: Reality itself is questioned through layered or looping structures that demand decoding.

tags.label: Ambiguous Ending
tags.definition: The ending deliberately withholds resolution, leaving key questions open.

tags.label: Twist-Driven
tags.definition: Sudden reversals redefine what the viewer thought was happening.

tags.label: Slow Burn
tags.definition: Tension accumulates patiently through long, deliberate scenes.

tags.label: Brisk
tags.definition: The story moves quickly with little dead air.

tags.label: Relentless
tags.definition: Unbroken pressure with almost no breathing room.

tags.label: Dialogue-Driven
tags.definition: Long, sharp conversations carry the film more than events.

tags.label: Visually Stylized
tags.definition: Distinctive, expressive visual design is a defining signature.

tags.label: Minimalist
tags.definition: Sparse means, restraint and understatement in presentation.

tags.label: Satirical
tags.definition: Social or institutional mockery via irony and exaggeration.

tags.label: Gritty
tags.definition: Grimy, unsentimental realism in texture and tone.

tags.label: Poetic
tags.definition: Lyrically composed images and narration over plain storytelling.

tags.label: Meta-Ironic
tags.definition: Self-aware irony about the medium itself and genre conventions.

tags.label: Found Footage
tags.definition: Presented as discovered raw recordings, with rough handheld immediacy.
